subject.title: [Feature]: sessions_kill should terminate all child exec processes spawned by a session

question: What public session exec-control contract and authorization boundary should OpenClaw expose for listing and terminating child exec processes spawned by a stored session?
rationale: The missing behavior is source-proven, but process visibility and termination can cross agent/session boundaries and needs maintainer-owned security semantics before implementation.

options.title: Add guarded session exec-control surface
options.body: Create new additive Gateway/CLI methods for session exec list and kill with explicit operator scope, canonical session resolution, per-run outcomes, and child/PTY/sandbox fallback tests.

options.title: Extend existing maintenance methods
options.body: Add explicit opt-in kill flags to existing session abort/delete methods while preserving current defaults and documenting upgrade behavior.

options.title: Defer public process control
options.body: Keep the existing agent-scoped process tool only and handle orphan/restart cleanup through narrower lifecycle issues until a broader design is ready.

recommendation.title: Add guarded session exec-control surface
recommendation.body: Create new additive Gateway/CLI methods for session exec list and kill with explicit operator scope, canonical session resolution, per-run outcomes, and child/PTY/sandbox fallback tests.

likelyOwner.reason: Vincent has strong recent history across process supervisor and session-adjacent code and is already connected to the issue timeline.
